title: AgentScope
summary: Offline preflight that shows which AI coding-agent instruction files apply to a repository path and in what order.
problem: Repositories increasingly contain several AI-agent instruction formats and nested scopes, making it hard to know which rules affect a particular file before an agent runs.
audience: Developers using Codex, GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, or mixed coding-agent workflows in one repository.
why_now: GitHub documents layered repository, path-specific, and agent instructions, while Codex added repository review rules in AGENTS.md in July 2026.
difference: AgentScope is a read-only offline path preflight: it maps applicable files without starting an agent, changing configuration, or syncing instruction content.
monetization_hypothesis: Best suited as a free local developer utility; a paid team policy-audit layer would need separate validation.
limitations: It models documented GitHub Copilot precedence and common root agent files, not every vendor's complete runtime behavior.
It does not interpret natural-language contradictions inside instruction text.

alternatives.name: GitHub Copilot instruction references
alternatives.difference: Copilot shows applied instruction references inside its own workflow; AgentScope can inspect scope offline before any agent session starts.

alternatives.name: rulesync
alternatives.difference: rulesync synchronizes or converts rule files across tools; AgentScope is read-only and only reports what applies to one target path.
